newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France could buy Boeing - paper.
newsitem.headline: Air France could buy Boeing - paper.

text.p: Christian Blanc, chairman of French state-owned airline Air France, said the company could possibly buy Boeing 777 planes instead of aircraft from its traditional supplier Airbus.

In an interview wIth the Les Echos newspaper Blanc said that despite the rise in oil prices the group still expected to break even this financial year and he confirmed his interest in acquiring small French airline AOM.
"Airbus is a formidable succes and an exemplary European company. For Air France it is the plane maker by reference," Blanc said.

However he added that the airline was making comparisons and calculations for its fleet acquisitions which the group could resume after having bought its last planes in 1993 before its financial crises forced it to cut spending.
A board meeting is scheduled for November 20 to discuss expansion of the long-range fleet.
"Today like yesterday, we need both Airbus and Boeing. Contrary to rumours circulating these past few weeks, our acquisition programme is balanced and involves both plane makers," he said.

He said he did not expect opposition from the government if the board decided to take the Boeing 777 planes as well as additional Airbus A340 suchs as the stretched Airbus A340-600 for which it could be the launch customer.
Junior Transport Minister Anne-Marie Idrac declined to say in an interview with RTL radio on Thursday morning whether the government would oppose a decision to buy Boeing planes.
Blanc said Air France still expected to break-even this financial year.

"I have pleasure in telling you about something which is going better, much better -- Air France. Despite the rise in fuel prices we maintain our objective of break-even this financial year," he said.
Blanc told Les Echos that it was important for airlines to control their hub.

"In the war for the hubs our English friends British Airways Plc have scored a nice goal. They have increased their network in France to feed their centre of operations in London (via the acquisition of Air Liberte). And they are weakening our position," he said.

"We are not in a situation of protectionism versus free competition. To win the battle of the big European companies, you have, as does Britush Airways or Lufthansa, to seal your hub, control your interior market and attack aggressively the natural markets of your neighbours," Blanc said.
"Who does not do that is certain to lose," he added.

"Taking account of what I have said, how do you believe that Air France and its shareholder could be indifferent to the possibility that AOM could also fall in the hands of British Airways?", Blanc said.
AOM is a regional airline put up for sale by the Consortium de Realisation (CDR) which is selling former Credit Lyonnais assets.
